data.title: Easier QR code payments, smoother online checkouts to come with enhanced PayNow
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Consumers can look forward to easier QR code payments here and a smoother online shopping checkout process as enhancements to the PayNow instant payments system are rolled out progressively from 2027.

Tourists visiting Singapore and Singaporeans travelling overseas can also expect more payment options as links between local and regional QR payment networks are expanded through the enhanced SGQR+.

These proposed enhancements and their implementation road map were outlined in the PayNow Generation 2 Phase 2 report released by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) on Nov 18.

The first phase examined how PayNow has evolved since its 2017 launch, with findings released in June. The second phase has identified seven enhancements to address gaps identified in the review, to be made between 2027 and 2028.

Through the enhanced SGQR+, Singaporeans and tourists will be able to pay with their preferred apps without having to check which QR schemes are accepted by the merchant, as Singapore connects to more major regional QR networks through SGQR+.

This will also enable more Singapore merchants to accept payments from tourists through a wider pool of foreign payment networks and Singaporeans to pay through local apps in more countries.

Development of the SGQR+ switch, which will provide an additional connection between participating schemes rather than require merchants or payment providers to replace their existing arrangements, is already under way.

A limited roll-out in 2027 will connect an initial group of participating schemes and test live payment journeys before expanding in scope in 2028.

Another key enhancement is deep-linking. Already live in Lazada checkouts via the OCBC app, it seamlessly opens shoppers’ preferred payment app when they select PayNow when checking out on an e-commerce platform. This eliminates the need to screenshot or download QR codes and retrieve them in the payment app from their phone gallery.

Higher PayNow limits will also allow Singaporeans to make and receive larger government payments with instant confirmation. The enhancement will first be introduced in late 2027 with one government agency, which has not been identified, before being progressively rolled out to other agencies from 2028.

Singapore currently applies a $200,000 limit for PayNow, which constrains its use for some high-value payments, such as property down payment or full payments for cars, above this threshold.

Clearer and more consistent rules will also be developed to address payment disputes, refunds, fraud and scams that may arise from individuals’ PayNow transactions to merchants.

This could offer customers and merchants a more consistent dispute resolution experience, with clearer processes and potentially faster resolution in certain cases, particularly those involving technical issues.

Such safeguards will be introduced in stages over 2028 by the Singapore Payments Network (SPaN), which was set up in 2025 by MAS and ABS to oversee Singapore’s national and cross-border payment schemes.

MAS will bring together SPaN, Banking Computer Services and other key partners to innovate new payment capabilities for emerging use cases, including AI agent-initiated payments.

Industry participants, including ABS, banks and payment service providers, will also test ways to process very large numbers of frequent micro-payments more cheaply.

OCBC said it has already enabled PayNow deep-linking with platforms such as Lazada, Pinduoduo, AXS, Frasers Mall and AnyWheel, as well as government agencies like the CPF Board for a more seamless checkout experience.

UOB said it is working with industry partners to explore some of the capabilities envisioned under the plans to enhance PayNow Generation 2, including how deep-linking and account-to-account payments can be more seamlessly integrated into online shopping journeys.

data.title: NETS pilots ‘tap QR to pay’; new app features make payments easier for tourists
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Consumers can soon use smartphones to complete purchases at NETS payment points – without scanning a QR code.

This was among the enhancements to the Nets app announced on Nov 18.

Nets is the first to pilot the tap QR facility to pay via SGQR.

This feature enables consumers to make payments simply by tapping their near-field communication (NFC)-enabled smartphones at participating Nets SGQR points, without first opening the app.

It offers a convenient alternative to the existing scan-to-pay method.

This initiative, to run for two months will be piloted in phases, starting in Toa Payoh in December. There are plans for a nationwide roll-out if the pilot is successful.

Tapping to pay via QR will initially be available through the Nets app, with support for other participating banking apps and wallets expected over time.

Nets’ chief executive Lawrence Chan said: “As usage expands, our priority is to make QR payments more accessible for everyone, including visitors to Singapore, while advancing interoperability across the payments ecosystem.”

The other new features on the app will also benefit groups such as tourists, said the payments services group.

From now, those whose home-country payment apps are not linked to Singapore’s single, standardised QR code, or SGQR, can also use the local payment ecosystem through the Nets app.

Visitors from countries with established QR cross-border linkages with Singapore, such as China, India and Indonesia, can continue to pay directly through their local bank or wallet apps.

The other enhancements include a family wallet, through which users can use sub-wallets to support the spending needs of their dependants.

The primary user can set a spending limit and be notified of the transactions in their sub-wallets. THE BUSINESS TIMES

data.title: Dollar holds near 19-month high as data supports case for US rate hikes
data.description:
TOKYO – The dollar held steady near a 19-month high on Nov 18 as US economic data and comments from Federal Reserve officials lent support to the case for interest rate hikes.

The yen held its ground after Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Kazuo Ueda reiterated the need to tighten policy further. The Australian dollar fell to a 10-month low ahead of a key jobs report on Nov 19.

Data on Nov 17 showed US retail sales increased moderately in October, reinforcing expectations for a rate hike in December.

Attention turns to US housing starts data due later on Nov 18 and a series of Fed speakers, ahead of the Nov 19 release of minutes of the central bank’s meeting in October, when it held rates steady.

“Overall, the report reinforces our view that further interest rate hikes from the Fed are warranted in order to counter demand-pull inflation,” Henry Russell, a London-based economist for ANZ, said about the US sales data. “The strength of domestic demand in the US, in our view, warrants a decisive monetary policy response from the Fed.”

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose 0.06% to 103.67. It touched 103.78 overnight, its highest level since April 2, 2025. The euro was down 0.14% at US$1.0982, while the yen edged up 0.08% to 159.25 per dollar. Sterling lost 0.13% to US$1.3191.

In addition to a 0.2% rise in retail sales that matched expectations, import prices climbed 1.1% in October compared with expectations for a 0.7% increase.

More US data is expected with the Census Bureau due to report housing starts data for October. Analysts are projecting an increase to 1.245 million from 1.221 million in September, while building permits likely decreased.

New York Fed president John Williams is expected to speak again following comments on Nov 17 when he said the Fed will likely need to raise interest rates further to contend with inflation. Fed Board governor Michael Barr and Minneapolis Fed president Neel Kashkari are also expected to speak at separate events.

Traders are pricing in a 95.7% chance that the Fed will raise its key rate by 25 basis points (bps) in December, the CME FedWatch tool showed. The odds of a 50-bp increase have fallen to 4.3%, from 13.5% a month ago.

“All Fed speakers are saying that the Fed should raise rates in an incremental way,” said Tapas Strickland, chief market strategist at Moomoo ANZ, on a podcast. “The reduction in the probability of a supersized move has resulted in a bit more stability re-emerging in markets.”

Markets got a measure of relief after Nvidia reported after the bell that third-quarter revenue doubled and forecast higher-than-estimated sales for the fourth quarter, boosting shares in Asia

The next major test of sentiment will be the market debut of AI bellwether Anthropic on Nov 19.

Japanese data on Nov 18 showed exports rose to a record monthly value in October on strong semiconductor-related demand. Also in Tokyo, BOJ governor Ueda said the central bank should continue raising interest rates, while stressing the need to anchor underlying inflation around its 2% target.

The Australian dollar sank 0.18% versus the greenback to US$0.6719 and earlier touched US$0.6718, its lowest point since Jan 19. Nov 18 data showed a surprise jump in wages, but labour figures on Nov 19 are considered more crucial to determining if the central bank will need to hike rates again.

The New Zealand dollar slid 0.07% to US$0.5488, nearing its 19-month low hit on Nov 17. REUTERS

data.title: Bank of Japan governor says central bank should keep raising rates
data.description:
TOKYO - Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Nov 18 that the central bank should continue raising interest rates, while stressing the need to anchor underlying inflation around its 2% target.

Speaking in Parliament, Ueda said it was important to see underlying inflation anchored around 2% over time and conduct monetary policy appropriately to ensure that this could be achieved.

“Given that financial conditions are still accommodative, it would be appropriate to continue raising the policy rate and adjust the degree of monetary easing in line with developments in the economy, prices and financial conditions,” Ueda said.

The BOJ kept interest rates steady at 1.25% at its Oct 30 meeting but declared victory in its 14-year battle to hit its price target and stressed its policy had entered a new phase focused on avoiding an inflation overshoot, reinforcing its hawkish bias.

Ueda said the planned consumption tax cut on food would likely support economic growth by boosting households’ real purchasing power, though the size of the impact would depend on factors such as companies’ pricing behaviour and consumer sentiment.

Once the details of the measure are finalised, the central bank will assess its impact on underlying inflation and reflect that analysis in future policy decisions, he added.

Asked about the possibility of emergency bond-buying operations, Ueda said the BOJ would make a comprehensive assessment based on conditions at the time, including whether serious disruptions to market functioning had emerged and required a policy response.

He also cautioned against using such operations to contain long-term yields, saying the move could prove counterproductive if markets perceive the BOJ as helping finance government spending.

“In that case, long-term interest rates could become even more volatile,” he said. REUTERS

data.title: Nvidia delivers strong results as investors weigh post-Huang future​
data.description:
SAN FRANCISCO - Nvidia forecast quarterly revenue above Wall Street estimates on Nov 17, giving investors some relief after longtime leader Jensen Huang’s resignation plunged the chip firm into crisis.

Shares of the company rose nearly 4% in extended trading but remained down about 17% for the year through the Nov 17 close. The company is valued at roughly US$3.8 trillion (S$4.9 trillion).

“Our momentum is real,” interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress said, without addressing the leadership uncertainty. “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track.”

With Huang gone, investors are looking for clues about Nvidia’s future, from billions of dollars invested in cloud providers, suppliers and AI startups to who will ultimately lead the world’s most valuable chipmaker.

The AI boom’s most prolific salesman resigned last week after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two Nvidia employees.

US intelligence agencies are trying to determine the extent of Alice Huang’s ties to China’s Ministry of State Security and what information she may have passed to Beijing, according to two people familiar with the matter.

Huang’s exit ended three decades of founder-led control over Nvidia’s chip roadmap, customer deals and Washington ties, making execution a bigger risk than near-term AI demand, analysts say.

The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of US$130 billion, plus or minus 3%, above analysts’ average estimate of US$125.25 billion, according to LSEG data. Nvidia said the outlook assumes no data-center chip sales to China.

Adjusted gross margin is expected at 71% to 72%, compared with analysts’ estimate of 71.7%.

Finance chief Colette Kress is interim CEO, while the board considers internal and external candidates. A growing “Stand With Jensen” campaign has complicated the search, although the board is not considering Huang’s return, three people told Reuters on Nov 16. Huang said on Nov 17 he would be “honoured” to return if the board deemed it best.

Earlier on Nov 17, Nvidia’s board created a committee on national security and export controls, its first major governance move since Huang’s departure, as scrutiny grows over the chipmaker’s national security role.

Washington has also tightened licensing rules for chip shipments to South-east Asia and overseas data centers serving Chinese firms, while lawmakers prepare to question Huang, who had pushed for greater chip exports to China.

Investors were already uneasy about AI spending after Democrats’ midterm sweep fueled fears of tougher scrutiny and slower data-center expansion. They also want to know whether Nvidia’s next CEO will continue financing customers, a practice critics call circular.

The Nov 17 results offer a first read on Vera Rubin, Nvidia’s newest generation of AI processors and successor to Grace Blackwell. Nvidia said in August that Vera Rubin would account for about a fifth of data-center revenue in the October quarter and forecast 70% revenue growth in the next fiscal year.

Nvidia’s third-quarter revenue more than doubled to US$115.84 billion, beating analysts’ estimate of $109.11 billion. The company has topped Wall Street’s revenue expectations for 17 straight quarters.

Adjusted gross margin rose to 74.9% from 73.5% a year earlier, also beating analysts’ estimate of 74.1%, despite soaring memory prices and production ramps. REUTERS

data.title: Don’t give AI agents your financial accounts login details, warns MAS chief Chia Der Jiun
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Consumers should avoid giving artificial intelligence agents their financial accounts’ login credentials, as there are insufficient safeguards to ensure that such tools act safely and within their users’ instructions, said Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) managing director Chia Der Jiun.

Speaking at the Singapore Fintech Festival on Nov 19, Chia noted that some payment services providers and financial institutions are building agent interfaces into their offerings, but many financial institutions have yet to establish terms or channels for agents to access financial services.

“There are some challenges here,” he said. “The financial institution does not know if this is an agent that is acting on the full authorisation and control of the customer, nor whether the agent is transacting within its mandate and instructions.

“If agents transact incorrectly or beyond their instruction, who bears responsibility?”

Chia said a trusted protocol and secure channel are needed for AI agents to access financial services, pointing to lessons from the first phase of MAS’ Safeguards for Agentic Finance at Runtime (SAFR) initiative.

These include ensuring that AI agents have sufficient autonomy to perform useful tasks while operating within clearly defined boundaries.

Their identities and authority to act on behalf of users must also be established, while their instructions should clearly specify what actions they can take, along with any limits and conditions.

“The greater the discretion and impact of action given an agent, the stronger the assurance and controls needed,” said Chia. 

MAS will also develop a common “know your agent” protocol for trusted information exchange between customer agents and financial institutions.

The protocol, part of the new phase of SAFR, will provide financial institutions with information on who the agent is and whom the agent represents, what authority it has been given, what mandate it operates under, and its origins and reliability.

“This will allow financial institutions to determine the terms and scope permitted to an agent, and establish a dedicated secure channel for agent access,” said Chia. 

Separately, MAS will set up a sandbox with the Future of Finance Institute to bring together AI agents and programmable money, focusing on two use cases: corporate treasury management and payment services.

For corporate treasury management, banks could allow an AI agent to monitor a company’s liquidity positions and due payments, decide when and where funds should move, and use tokenised deposits to execute permitted treasury actions.

Companies would set the mandates for their agents, while participating banks would set the controls and determine the terms for accepting each agent instruction.

For payment services, banks and payment service providers could allow customer agents to execute payment instructions using digital money, such as tokenised deposits or stablecoins.

Participating banks and payment service providers would verify the agents’ identities and authority, and apply risk controls before executing the transactions.

“The two use cases, and others that we will collaborate on in the future, would provide important lessons on the benefits and safeguards of such transactions,” said Chia.

“Consumers and businesses need to retain meaningful control over the objectives, mandate and actions of their agents.

“Autonomy has to be bounded. Actions and outcomes have to come with accountability,” he added.

MAS also announced on Nov 19 that it had successfully issued $100 million of tokenised MAS Bills on Nov 6.

The four-week MAS Bills were issued on the Singapore Dollar Test Network and settled using wholesale central bank digital currency (CBDC).

Five primary dealers – DBS, HSBC, OCBC, Standard Chartered and UOB – participated in the issuance auction, with applications amounting to more than double the issuance size.

The tokenised MAS Bills will mature on Dec 4.

MAS said it intends to scale up tokenised MAS Bills issuances, bring on board more participating financial institutions and expand their use for collateral management.

Interested financial institutions and financial market infrastructure providers can be involved in the next phase of live trials in 2027, it added.

data.title: One app, many ways to pay: How DBS is shaping the next wave of digital payments with PayLah!
data.description:
For millions of Singaporeans, paying with DBS PayLah! has become part of their daily routines – from buying meals at hawker centres to paying at heartland shops and malls.

What began as a peer-to-peer mobile wallet more than a decade ago has grown into one of Singapore’s most widely used payment platforms, with over three million users.

DBS is now building on this foundation, extending the convenience of PayLah! beyond Singapore’s shores and into more payment situations. From shops across the Causeway to storefronts in China, PayLah! users can scan to pay just as they do at Singapore’s hawker centres – where PayLah! accounts for more than 60 per cent of QR transactions.

“The way people pay has evolved significantly over the past decade, and so have their expectations. Today, customers value not just the ability to pay digitally, but how simple and seamless the experience is,” said Chan Sow Han, head of Payments and Unsecured Lending at DBS Singapore.

“Our focus is to build on what customers already know and use, extending that ease of payment across more situations and locations so they can use PayLah! to pay wherever they are, while continuing to enhance the experience to better serve their needs.”

Making payments anywhere

QR payments are widely used across Asia, but payment systems and practices differ across markets. In China, for instance, customers may scan a merchant’s QR code or present their own for the cashier to scan.

DBS is addressing this through its latest expansion of PayLah!, which enables users to make QR payments at over 100 million participating Alipay+ and Weixin Pay merchants across China.

On top of existing UnionPay QR connectivity, DBS is the first and only bank in Singapore to support both payment methods across China’s three major QR payment ecosystems.

The development marks another milestone in DBS’ efforts to extend the payment habits Singaporeans are accustomed to at home across international borders. According to DBS, in 2022, it became the first bank in Singapore to enable consumers to make QR payments globally using a local app, through its partnership with UnionPay International.

Since then, PayLah!’s overseas reach has grown through partnerships with payment networks. These include DuitNow in Malaysia, PromptPay in Thailand and QRIS in Indonesia, allowing customers to scan to pay when travelling to these destinations. This year, DBS said it also became the first Singapore bank to connect to Taiwan’s TWQR network, allowing PayLah! users to scan to pay at over 250,000 participating merchants in Taiwan.

“While QR payments are increasingly common across Asia, different markets have their own payment systems and ways of transacting. Our approach has been to work with established payment networks and partners to bridge these differences, so customers can enjoy a more consistent payment experience when travelling,” said Chan.

These efforts have translated into growing customer usage. Last year, PayLah!’s cross-border QR transaction volumes have grown 2.5 times year-on-year, while the number of unique users has doubled. Average spending per customer on PayLah!’s overseas QR transactions has also increased by approximately 30 per cent in the same period.

Recognising that customers have different payment preferences when travelling, DBS also introduced the TravelLah! Debit Card in September 2026, complementing PayLah!’s overseas QR payment capabilities with a debit card option.

Available to customers aged 16 and above, TravelLah! offers zero foreign exchange fees, using Visa exchange rates without additional mark-ups from DBS. Customers can pay in more than 150 currencies worldwide and view indicative exchange rates directly on the PayLah! app, giving them greater visibility over prevailing rates before they spend.

TravelLah! also offers zero DBS fees on overseas ATM withdrawals, with no cap on the amount or frequency of overseas withdrawals.

The accompanying TravelLah! Debit Card Wallet within DBS PayLah! held in Singapore dollars can be topped up as needed, allowing customers to set aside funds for their travels without having to pre-convert or manage multiple currencies. Cardholders can also redeem complimentary basic travel insurance, subject to terms and conditions.

The card has attracted interest among younger customers, with around half of those who signed up in its first month aged between 16 and 29.

Designed for every stage of life

Beyond expanding where and how customers can pay, DBS is also enhancing PayLah! to better serve the needs of different customer groups.

“With a user base spanning different generations and life stages, we recognise that what customers expect from a payment app can vary considerably,” Chan explains. “A teenager learning to manage an allowance has different needs from a young adult travelling overseas or a senior who values simplicity when making digital payments.”

Rather than offering the same experience to everyone, DBS is moving towards a more personalised PayLah! experience, where customers can more easily access the features, offers and rewards most relevant to them.

For younger customers, DBS PayLah! for Teens, introduced in April 2026, offers an age-appropriate payment experience, including the ability to receive allowances digitally, customise transfer limits, and access relevant coupons and rewards. It also comes with built-in safeguards, including disabled auto-debit and spending controls, to help teenagers gain confidence in making digital payments safely.

A new senior-friendly mode was also launched last month, offering a simpler setup, with larger text, clearer navigation and easy access to core payment functions.

PayLah! also makes it easier for customers to get more value from their everyday spending. Those with DBS/POSB cards that earn DBS Points or POSB Daily$ can use their points to redeem a wide variety of rewards, including instantly offsetting eligible transactions, exchanging points for cash credits or Flexi eVouchers which can be used at NETS merchants across Singapore.

Beyond tailoring the experience to different users, DBS has also simplified everyday payment journeys, including online shopping through PayLah! Express Checkout. The feature enables customers to link their account once and subsequently complete purchases on participating platforms such as Lazada, foodpanda and Gojek. This allows customers to pay without switching between apps or entering card details on individual platforms.

Greater control and peace of mind

Backed by DBS, PayLah! combines the convenience of an everyday wallet with safeguards and customer controls that help customers manage their spending and transact with greater confidence.

To further safeguard customers, DBS will soon introduce complimentary wallet protection for all PayLah! users, providing coverage against unauthorised third-party transactions.

Looking ahead, DBS will continue expanding PayLah!’s payment capabilities while making the experience more personalised and rewarding.

“As we expand PayLah!’s capabilities, our focus is not simply on adding more features, but on making the experience more relevant to customers’ needs. We want them to derive greater value from each interaction, while retaining the simplicity and convenience they value,” said Chan.

data.title: After US$6.3 billion crypto heist, Binance plans foray into 5 Asian markets
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, plans to expand into five Asian markets in 2027 with South and South-east Asia as key priorities, its regional business head said, not long after the firm was hit with a record US$6.3 billion (S$8.1 billion) digital heist in October.

“We have ongoing conversations with at least five or six markets... three of which are in quite mature stages,” S.B. Seker told Reuters on the sidelines of the Singapore FinTech Festival on Nov 18. “The others are ongoing conversations.”

He did not specify the new markets that Binance, which currently has operating licences in more than 10 jurisdictions, was looking at, but said details of the planned expansion were expected to be rolled out in the first quarter of 2027.

Binance’s expansion plans come on the heels of a security breach linked to North Korea that resulted in US$6.3 billion being stolen from its platform in October.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation and Binance have said North Korea was responsible for the hack, but Pyongyang has denied that.

The company, which resumed withdrawals in phases earlier in November after covering 95% of the lost tokens, said last weekend it aimed to reopen withdrawals for all remaining networks and assets by the end of this week.

The Binance heist, which has been described by experts as the largest crypto theft ever, has renewed scrutiny of inconsistent security practices in the industry.

Seker, the firm’s head of APAC, said Binance contacted a number of regulators, including those in Japan, South Korea, Australia, Thailand and New Zealand, within the first 36 to 48 hours of the incident, to address questions about the scale of its impact and how the attack unfolded.

“Think of all the financial services regulators and markets where we are present,” he said, adding that there was no one country that led the charge in the investigations.

Binance says the Abu Dhabi Global Market’s Financial Services Regulatory Authority is its primary regulator.

Seker said that while discussions with regulators were ongoing, the conversation had moved beyond the heist to broader concerns about security threats facing the crypto industry.

“The conversations now are ‘Well, this is an omnipresent and spectrum-wide threat, and how does an entire ecosystem prepare for this?’ It’s moved away from the original incident to a much broader conversation,” he said.

“We are part of the conversation, but we are not driving the conversation in isolation anymore.” REUTERS

data.title: UN says Singapore’s Penguin International broke Libya arms embargo; company disputes panel’s findings
data.description:
SINGAPORE - Singapore-listed shipbuilder Penguin International has disputed a United Nations panel’s finding that its sale of two vessels subsequently shipped to Libya violated an arms embargo, saying the vessels were built for commercial use and delivered without weapons.

In a bourse filing on Nov 17, the company said the transaction involved a security vessel and a landing craft sold in December 2024 to Dubai-based 2020 Volume Boats.

Both vessels were delivered from Penguin’s yard in Singapore, and then shipped to Benghazi, Libya.

On Mar 24, 2026, the UN Panel of Experts on Libya published a report naming Penguin and its wholly owned subsidiary, Penguin Shipyard Asia.

The panel classified the security vessel as a naval-type fast patrol vessel and the landing craft as a dual-use vessel, and considered their transfer to Libya a violation of an arms embargo imposed under UN Security Council Resolution 1970.

However, the panel did not recommend sanctions against Penguin or its subsidiary.

Penguin said it disagreed with the panel’s characterisation of the vessels and its conclusion that the transaction breached the arms embargo.

The company maintained that both vessels had been designed and built for commercial purposes and were delivered without arms or ammunition on board.

Penguin said it had corresponded with the UN panel between January and May in 2025 and provided the information requested in relation to the transaction.

It became aware of the panel’s report in September 2026, about six months after its publication, and subsequently engaged Singapore legal counsel and an international sanctions specialist to assess the implications.

Based on the advice received, Penguin said being named in the report did not itself constitute a sanctions action or impose any direct penalties.

The company also understood that the likelihood of the UN imposing sanctions against Penguin or its subsidiary on the basis of the report was low.

Separately, Penguin has been corresponding with Singapore Customs since November 2025 regarding the export of the vessels.

The company said the matter had not materially disrupted its operations, and its board was not presently aware of any material financial impact. THE BUSINESS TIMES

data.title: Indonesia resumes rate hikes to defend rupiah, more tightening seen
data.description:
JAKARTA – Indonesia’s central bank unexpectedly raised its policy rate on Nov 18, resuming a tightening cycle intended to put a floor under the rupiah after the currency hit multiple record lows in the past week amid domestic political turmoil.

Analysts said the move is unlikely to be the last, with persistent external pressures and concerns over Indonesia’s market appeal expected to keep the central bank on a tightening path into 2027.

Bank Indonesia (BI) raised the benchmark seven-day reverse repurchase rate to 6%, the highest since January 2025, matching the prediction of 10 of 27 economists polled by Reuters. The rest had expected a hold.

Its overnight deposit facility and lending facility rates were also increased by the same amount to 5.25% and 6.75%, respectively.

BI has now raised the benchmark rate by 125 basis points since May to defend the rupiah, currently the worst-performing among emerging Asian currencies.

The rupiah touched an all-time low of 18,285 per US dollar on Nov 17 and has traded near that level since.

Governor Destry Damayanti said the hike was a “pre-emptive” move to ensure the inflation rate stays within BI’s target range and to maintain the attractiveness of rupiah assets in anticipation of a US rate hike in December.

“Going forward, BI will continue to consistently direct its monetary policy to strengthen the stability of the rupiah exchange rate in order to keep inflation within target,” Destry said.

The rupiah has been under pressure for most of 2026 on concerns over fiscal discipline and political interference in the central bank.

It weakened further last week after Indonesia’s Vice-President resigned and four senior police officers implicated in an illegal wiretapping, including of the President’s phone.

Growing complexity of problems

The rupiah’s depreciation has so far had limited impact on inflation, which eased slightly to 3.23% in October, within BI’s 1.5% to 3.5% target range. The government caps fuel prices through subsidies to keep inflation under control.

Senior Deputy Governor Aida Budiman said the rate decision would ensure inflation stays within target in the next two years.

The rupiah barely moved after the policy decision.

Destry said the central bank’s other measures, including a 200 basis point cut in reserve requirements announced in October, would help offset the impact of higher rates on liquidity, bank lending and economic growth.

Some analysts have described BI’s October policy announcement as perplexing. Asked about its policy stance, Destry said BI’s policy mix was innovative, designed to address “problems that are increasingly complex”.

Indonesia’s economic growth accelerated in the third quarter to 5.47%, data showed earlier in November, from 5.29% in the previous three months.

That, however, remained far slower than President Prabowo Subianto’s 8% target by 2029.

Persistent external pressures, concerns about a potential downgrade by MSCI for Indonesia’s stock market and political uncertainty may extend BI’s tightening cycle into 2027, analysts said.

Barclays predicted BI would resume tightening to reach a terminal benchmark rate of 6.75% in the middle of 2027.

Jakarta-based Bank Permata expected the benchmark at 6.50% by the end of 2027.

Consultancy firm Capital Economics also expected the main rate to be at 6.5% by the end of 2027, with investors monitoring if BI would deliver more hikes, economist Jason Tuvey said.

“Investors will be watching closely for any comments from government officials regarding today’s decision by the central bank given their push for faster economic growth,” he said.

“The acid test for Bank Indonesia will be how it responds if the rupiah were to come under fresh downward pressure in the coming months,” Tuvey said. REUTERS

data.title: MindChamps founder seeks $86m for first pre-school fund to expand in Australia
data.description:
The founder of Singapore-listed MindChamps Preschool has launched an investment platform that is seeking to raise A$100 million (S$86.2 million) for its first fund to acquire and develop purpose-built pre-school properties in Australia.

The platform, MindFunds, will pursue investments across the education sector, David Chiem, founder of MindChamps, a franchiser of pre-school centres, said in an interview. The company has sold 45 franchise licences as part of its expansion in Australia, and the fund will acquire or develop properties where franchisees can open and operate their centres, he said.

MindChamps is targeting a first close for the fund in the first half of 2027, according to Goh Seh Harn, chief executive officer of Trigger Asset Management, who advises on the fund. It also plans a follow-on fund of A$500 million, he said.

Across Asia, growing demand for quality education has fuelled a rush of private capital into schools, opening up new sources of funding for a sector that has traditionally relied on equity and bank loans. Financiers such as Apollo Global Management and KKR & Co have bought stakes and lent money to school chains, betting that rising incomes and families’ willingness to spend more on their children will spur expansion.

MindChamps operates pre-schools, after-school care centres and therapy services for children. The Singapore-based company has also expanded its presence into markets including Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Myanmar. BLOOMBERG

data.title: Asia stocks choppy after Nvidia earnings as Anthropic pricing looms
data.description:
SINGAPORE – Stocks erased early gains in Asia on Nov 18 after Nvidia posted a better-than-expected sales forecast, as investor confidence remained fragile over questions about the company’s future leadership and potential impacts on its regional supply chain.

In choppy trade, MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan reversed an initial rally to be down 0.1%, narrowly extending its losing streak into a fifth day.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 slid 0.3%, while US S&P 500 e-mini futures clung to gains, up 0.3%.

Despite Nvidia’s upbeat earnings, strategists noted that deeper concerns over the sustainability of AI capital expenditure remain.

Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank in Singapore, said: “Nvidia’s results were reassuring and gave investors a reason to refocus on earnings, but they haven’t resolved the broader questions around AI spending returns, financing sustainability and leadership uncertainty.

“So we are seeing an initial relief rally, but not necessarily the conviction needed for a sustained recovery.”

In oil markets, Brent crude futures were 0.6% lower at US$92.60 a barrel in Asian trade, following data showing an increase in US crude and fuel inventories last week.

The ongoing Middle East conflict and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, however, limited losses.

Referendum on AI

Nvidia shares slid 0.5% in after-hours trading, after rising as much as 3.8% following the chipmaker’s third-quarter revenue report and a fourth-quarter forecast that beat market expectations.

The tech company’s earnings report was its first since Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure as chief executive officer in November.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is probing Nvidia, citing sources familiar with the matter. The SEC has declined to comment on the matter.

“We’re at a point of peak uncertainty because investors still don’t know what Nvidia’s long-term leadership will look like,” said Brian Colello, senior equity analyst at Morningstar.

Overnight, stocks on Wall Street sold off again, with the S&P 500 down 1% to log a fourth consecutive session lower prior to Nvidia’s earnings report.

“Risk sentiment remained firmly on the defensive overnight, with the tech-led sell-off extending across global markets,” Westpac analysts said in a note.

“I’ve looked at this whole week as a referendum on AI,” said Jake Behan, head of capital markets at Direxion in New York.

“Nvidia gave us a read on the buildout, and Anthropic is about to give us a read on investor appetite for the next generation of AI companies.”

Overnight, stocks on Wall Street sold off again, with the S&P 500 down 1% to log a fourth consecutive session lower prior to Nvidia’s earnings report.

The next health check on the AI industry will come as Anthropic prepares to price its shares later on Nov 18 ahead of its market debut, which could value the company at as much as US$1.4 trillion (S$1.8 trillion).

The company has guided its initial public offering price to the top of its range or above, Bloomberg News reported.
